title: Pasta alla Norma
subtitle: Sicilian rigatoni with fried aubergine and tomato sauce
excerpt: Rigatoni tossed with a rich tomato sauce and fried cubes of aubergine, finished with creamy ricotta and torn basil. Named after a Bellini opera and beloved across Sicily.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla Norma originated in Catania, Sicily, and is named in honour of the opera Norma by Vincenzo Bellini, himself a Catanian. Traditionally made with salted ricotta, fresh ricotta makes a fine alternative.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made a day ahead. Fry the aubergine fresh before serving.

content.text: Fry the aubergine in plenty of oil until golden; undercooked aubergine is spongy and bitter.
Salt the aubergine cubes and leave in a colander for 10 minutes. Pat dry.
Heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Fry the aubergine in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on all sides. Drain on kitchen paper.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in the large saucepan over a medium heat.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until the garlic is just golden.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Crush them with a spoon. Season and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the rigatoni in a large pot of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.
Add the fried aubergine to the tomato sauce. Stir in half the basil.
Drain the pasta and add it to the sauce. Toss well, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed.
Serve topped with dollops of ricotta and the remaining basil.

items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or too many pieces at once.
items.fix: Fry in smaller batches over higher heat.

items.cause: Simmered too long or tinned tomatoes were very dry.
items.fix: Loosen with reserved pasta water, one splash at a time.

items.cause: Pasta water was not salted enough.
items.fix: Season pasta water heavily; it should taste like mild seawater.
